name: Physical Contradiction (TRIZ)
description: One parameter must be A and ¬A — resolution via four separation principles
whenToUse: When a single parameter would have to hold two opposite values at the same time and the contradiction is to be resolved by separation in time, space, condition or system level — not for a contradiction between two different characteristics, which is what the contradiction matrix is for.
requirementALabel: should be A, in order to …
requirementAPlaceholder: e.g. long — for high lift at take-off
requirementNotAPlaceholder: e.g. short — for low drag at cruise
problemNotePlaceholder: Background, boundary conditions, cross-reference to contradiction matrix or 9-Windows …
separationHint: For each principle, note whether and how it can be applied to the case. Then pick the principle that fits.
principleNotePlaceholder: How could this principle be applied to the contradiction at hand?
solutionPlaceholder: Derive the concrete solution from the chosen principle — what changes when / where / under which condition / at which level?

time.name: Separation in time
time.question: Can the parameter take different values at different moments?
time.example: Folding wing — long for take-off, short at cruise. Also: landing gear, airbag, saw blade (cut vs. return stroke).

space.name: Separation in space
space.question: Can the parameter take different values in different regions of the system?
space.example: Screw — hard head, elastic shaft. Also: drill bit sharp at the tip, progressive eyeglass lenses.

condition.name: Separation on condition
condition.question: Can the parameter take different values depending on load, temperature, speed, user …?
condition.example: Non-Newtonian fluid — liquid at rest, solid under impact. Also: photochromic glasses, memory foam, ABS.

system.name: Separation between system levels
system.question: Does the contradiction dissolve when you switch between sub-, system and supersystem?
system.example: Bicycle chain — flexible as a whole, rigid in each link. Also: stranded wire (thin threads, thick strand), sandwich composites.
